_note: Water the land mask has to be told about.
scripts/build-landmask.mjs marks a cell as land when land touches it ANYWHERE in
the cell — the rule that finally made Brac, Capri and Cape Cod visible. It cuts
both ways: a channel narrower than a 3.7 km cell is walled off by the same
honesty, and a few of those channels are among the most heavily used water on
earth. The Bosphorus is 700 m across. The Suez Canal is 300 m. The Corinth Canal
is twenty-one metres.
So this file reopens them. It is an exception list, not a tuning knob: every
entry is a named canal or strait that ships genuinely transit, and the reason it
needs an entry is its width. Nothing here exists to make a route look nicer.
The old 0.1-degree mask left the Bosphorus open by accident rather than by
intent, which is why removing this file would silently strand the entire Black
Sea — Istanbul, Odessa and Constanta — 240 km from the nearest water the router
believes in.
`line` is a polyline of [lat, lng] following the channel; `widthCells` is the
half-width carved either side, so 1 clears a three-cell corridor (~11 km).
NOT here, deliberately: the estuary berths that sit tens of kilometres up a
river — London, Hamburg, Antwerp, Bordeaux, Seville, Montreal. Those were out of
reach of the old mask too, at 77-272 km, and a river is not a strait. They snap
to the nearest coastal water, which is what a sea atlas should draw.

passages.name: Bosphorus
passages.why: The only way into the Black Sea. Without it Istanbul, Odessa and Constanta are unreachable.

passages.name: Dardanelles
passages.why: The other half of the Turkish Straits: the Sea of Marmara reaches the Aegean through here or not at all.

passages.name: Suez Canal
passages.why: Mediterranean to Red Sea. It survives rasterisation today only because Natural Earth happens to leave a gap there, which is luck rather than a guarantee.

passages.name: Panama Canal
passages.why: Atlantic to Pacific, and the spine of the atlas's Central America & Panama region.

passages.name: Corinth Canal
passages.why: Saronic Gulf to Gulf of Corinth. Too narrow for cruise ships and routinely transited by the yachts this atlas sells.

passages.name: Strait of Messina
passages.why: Between Sicily and the toe of Italy — the difference between Naples to Taormina being a hop and being a circumnavigation of Sicily.

passages.name: Stockholm archipelago
passages.why: Stockholm is a scheduled Baltic port and the fairway to it threads islands far narrower than a cell.

passages.name: Haro Strait and Boundary Pass
passages.width: about 3 km between Stuart Island and Saturna
passages.why: Juan de Fuca to the Strait of Georgia. Rasterised shut by the Gulf and San Juan Islands, which left Vancouver and every Strait of Georgia port 35-145 km from the water the router believes in. Those ports snapped to the OUTER coast of Vancouver Island instead, and the leg was drawn as a straight line across the island.

passages.name: Admiralty Inlet
passages.width: about 5 km off Point No Point
passages.why: The only way into Puget Sound. Without it Seattle, a home port for Alaska sailings, sits 43 km from connected water and its legs begin on dry land.

passages.name: Johnstone Strait and Discovery Passage
passages.width: under 1 km at Seymour Narrows; 2-5 km along Johnstone Strait
passages.why: The Inside Passage behind Vancouver Island, Queen Charlotte Strait to the Strait of Georgia. Closed in the mask, so expedition ports in Desolation Sound and Johnstone Strait itself could only snap across the island to the open Pacific.

passages.name: Beagle Channel, Ushuaia to Puerto Williams
passages.why: Ushuaia is the busiest port in the expedition feed — the gateway for almost every Antarctic sailing — and the channel it sits on was rasterised shut, so every one of those routes began with a stub drawn across Tierra del Fuego or Navarino Island.

passages.name: Strait of Magellan, Primera and Segunda Angostura
passages.width: about 3 km at the First Narrows
passages.why: The narrows cut Punta Arenas off from the Atlantic, so hops along the strait were routed 1,000+ km around Tierra del Fuego.

passages.name: Rio-Antirrio Strait
passages.why: The western mouth of the Gulf of Corinth. Closed, every Gulf port (Itea for Delphi) could only reach the Ionian Sea via the Corinth Canal and right round the Peloponnese.

passages.name: Kanmon Strait
passages.why: Between Honshu and Kyushu, the Inland Sea's western door. Closed, Shimonoseki to Moji — 9 km apart — was routed 1,000 km around Kyushu.
